Rossie D. Alston Jr.

and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

PLAINTIFE’S RULE 72(a) OBJECTIONS TO ECF NO. 84 AND MOTION TO SET
ASIDE THE AMENDMENT AND DISCOVERY DENIALS AND FOR COORDINATED
DETERMINATION OF THE PENDING OBJECTIONS

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine objects under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A), Federal Rule of
Civil Procedure 72(a), and Local Civil Rule 72 to the Order entered October 7, 2026 (ECF No. 84).
Local Civil Rule 72 treats these objections as a motion under Local Civil Rule 7. Plaintiff files them
in that form. A Memorandum in Support accompanies this Motion under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1)
and states the grounds. Plaintiff incorporates it by reference. No comparison document

accompanies this filing.

I. THE ORDER AND THE TWO DISPOSITIONS CHALLENGED
1. ECF No. 84 was signed by Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis and entered October 7, 2026.

It makes two dispositions.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 89 _ Filed 10/13/26 Page 2 of 12 PagelD# 871

2. Discovery. ECF No. 84 denies “as premature” Plaintiff’s Motion for Leave to Serve
Three Limited Interrogatories on NCMEC before the Rule 26(f) Conference (ECF No. 15) and
Plaintiff’s Motion for Leave to Serve Four Limited Interrogatories on Meta Platforms, Inc. before
the Rule 26(f) Conference (ECF No. 54). ECF No. 84 at 1. The Order states: “At this time, the
Court cannot issue an order concerning Plaintiff’s Motions because discovery has not officially
begun in this case. Pursuant to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, discovery officially begins
when the District Judge issues a Scheduling Order and currently there is no Scheduling Order in
this case.” Id. at 1-2.

3. Amendment. ECF No. 84 denies Plaintiff’s Motion for Leave to File Second Amended
and Supplemental Complaint Pursuant to Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 15(a)(2) and 15(d), and
Request for Expedited Determination on the Papers (ECF No. 59). The Order states: “Plaintiff was
given ample opportunity to comply with the Court’s September 9, 2026 Order [Dkt. No. 64] by
producing a redlined Second Amended Complaint but has failed to do so as of the date of this
Order.” ECF No. 84 at 2.

4. The motions to dismiss filed by NCMEC (ECF No. 10), Meta (ECF No. 21), and Hall
(ECF No. 45) remain pending before the District Judge against the First Amended Complaint (ECF
No. 5).

II. THE OBJECTIONS

5. First objection: the discovery ruling rests on a legal premise the rule does not permit.
Rule 26(d)(1) bars discovery before the Rule 26(f) conference “except ... when authorized by
these rules, by stipulation, or by court order.” ECF Nos. 15 and 54 requested that court order. ECF
No. 84 treated the absence of a Scheduling Order and of ordinary discovery as preventing the Court
from issuing one. That premise removes the exception the motions invoked. The ruling is contrary

to law. It evaluated neither request under any standard for preconference discovery.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 89 Filed 10/13/26 Page 3 of 12 PagelD# 872

6. Second objection: the comparison condition must be reviewed together with its
enforcement. ECF No. 64 found that the Court “does not possess sufficient information to issue an
Order” on ECF No. 59, and required a marked comparison of the proposed pleading against the
original Complaint (ECF No. 1) by September 11, 2026. ECF No. 59 seeks to replace the First
Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5), not ECF No. 1. The complete proposed pleading (ECF No. 59-
1), a supporting declaration (ECF No. 59-2), and a memorandum identifying the material
amendments by category and section (ECF No. 60) were before the Court. Plaintiff’s objections to
the informational premise, the selected baseline, and the compliance period (ECF Nos. 66, 67, 68)
were pending and undecided when ECF No. 84 enforced the condition by denying ECF No. 59.

7. Third objection: the initial failure and the continued nonproduction required assessment
against the relief Plaintiff had requested. Plaintiff first received actual notice of ECF No. 64 at
about 9:09 p.m. on September 11, 2026, the compliance date. ECF No. 68-1 § 3-10. Two days
later Plaintiff sought review of the condition, suspension of its enforcement, relief from the expired
deadline under Rule 6(b)(1)(B), and a prospective compliance procedure keyed to a ruling on the
baseline. ECF No. 67 {{ 6-9. No comparison was produced through October 7, 2026. The requests
for relief were never decided. ECF No. 84 treated elapsed time as resolving them. Plaintiff objects
to the finding of “ample opportunity” to the extent it rests on a misunderstanding of the notice
chronology, and separately objects to the judgment that nonproduction justified denying a
completed Rule 15 submission on this record, without a warning in ECF No. 64 and without
addressing the less severe course already proposed.

8. Fourth objection: the rulings affect substantial rights. The amendment denial excludes
identified allegations and subsequent events from the pleading against which three dismissal

motions will be decided. ECF No. 59-1 §8§ O, P-S; ECF No. 60 at 7-15. The discovery denials

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 89 Filed 10/13/26 Page 4 of 12 PagelD# 873

reject seven closed answers about records Defendants control, on which Defendants’ dismissal
arguments rely, on the erroneous premise stated in the first objection. Fed. R. Civ. P. 61.

9. Fifth objection: statutory disqualification based on subsequently obtained financial
disclosures. Plaintiff separately objects to ECF No. 84 under 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4) and § 455(a).
The annual financial disclosure reports of Magistrate Judge Davis submitted as Exhibits A and B to
the concurrent Plaintiff’s Motion to Disqualify Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis Under 28 U.S.C. 8
455(b)(4) and 8 455(a), and for Priority Determination identify “FB common stock,” the reported
Meta interest, at year-end 2025 (Exhibit A) and year-end 2024 (Exhibit B). Plaintiff advances
continued qualifying ownership during the relevant participation as an inference requiring
determination, not as an established fact. Plaintiff was unaware of the reported interest when ECF
No. 84 was entered and presents this ground promptly after learning of it. Declaration of Marvelle
J. Ballentine in Support of Plaintiff’s Motion to Disqualify Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis {{ 2-4.
Plaintiff requests consideration of that Declaration and Exhibits A and B and vacatur of ECF No.
84 upon the necessary statutory and remedial findings, either on these objections or through the
concurrent targeted-vacatur application. This objection supplements, and does not replace, the
preceding four objections.

TI. STANDARD OF REVIEW AND ALTERNATIVE CLASSIFICATION

10. The District Judge “must consider timely objections and modify or set aside any part of
the order that is clearly erroneous or is contrary to law.” Fed. R. Civ. P. 72(a); 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)
(1)(A). The first objection presents legal error. The third presents a factual component and a
discretionary component. The second and fourth concern the exercise of discretion and its effect.
The fifth presents an additional statutory issue that requires consideration of the financial evidence
identified in paragraph 9 and a separate remedial determination under 28 U.S.C. § 455. To the

extent the Court treats any portion of ECF No. 84 as dispositive of a claim or defense, Plaintiff

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 89 Filed 10/13/26 Page 5 of 12 PagelD# 874

alternatively requests treatment of that portion under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(B)-(C) and de novo
determination under Rule 72(b)(3). Plaintiff does not contend that ECF No. 84 terminated any
claim.

IV. TIMELINESS, RELATED MATTERS, AND THE INDEPENDENCE OF THESE
OBJECTIONS
11. ECF No. 84 was entered October 7, 2026. The Court serves orders on Plaintiff by mail.

ECF No. 68-1 { 3. Plaintiff submitted this Motion through the Court’s Electronic Document
Submission System on October 13, 2026. That submission is within fourteen days of the entry date
itself, without the additional time Rule 6(d) provides for mail service. Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(1), 72(a).

12. Plaintiff’s Rule 72(a) Objections to ECF Nos. 63-65 (ECF No. 66), his Motion to Set
Aside ECF No. 64 (ECF No. 67), the Memorandum in Support (ECF No. 68), and his Motion for
Leave to File Notice of Subsequent Record Development (ECF No. 76) remain pending before the
District Judge. ECF Nos. 66 and 67 remain the vehicle challenging ECF Nos. 63, 64, and 65. These
objections challenge ECF No. 84. They do not restart the time to challenge the September orders,
and they withdraw nothing stated in ECF Nos. 66, 67, 68, or 76. On October 12, 2026, Plaintiff
submitted through the Court’s Electronic Document Submission System a Notice of Waiver of
Oral Argument as to ECF Nos. 66, 67, and 76, requesting determination of those motions on the
papers under Local Civil Rule 7(J).

13. Plaintiff concurrently presents a motion under 28 U.S.C. § 455 concerning the
Magistrate Judge’s disqualification and a motion to the District Judge for targeted vacatur and
withdrawal or modification of the referral. Those applications neither replace these objections nor
extend their filing period. The grounds and affirmative relief presented in these objections remain

independently maintained.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 89 Filed 10/13/26 Page 6 of 12 PagelD# 875

14. A separate Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument accompanies this Motion and requests
determination of these objections, this Motion, and the interim application on the papers. That
notice does not waive Plaintiff’s pending request to restore oral argument on ECF Nos. 15 and 54.
ECF No. 67 § 6(d).

V. INTERIM RELIEF REQUESTED
15. The filing of Rule 72(a) objections does not itself suspend the order objected to.

Plaintiff therefore requests an interim order, in the form of the accompanying Proposed Interim
Order, on an expedited basis. Each part is requested separately and may be granted without the
others:

(a) suspending enforcement of the comparison condition in ECF No. 64 pending the
Court’s determination of ECF Nos. 66, 67, 68, and 76 and of these objections;

(b) providing that, while that suspension operates, ECF No. 59 and the proposed pleading at
ECF No. 59-1 shall not be denied, stricken, deemed abandoned, excluded, or otherwise adversely
treated on the ground of nonproduction of the comparison directed by ECF No. 64;

(c) directing that the amendment-related issues presented in ECF Nos. 66, 67, and 76 and in
these objections be determined before, or expressly within, any disposition of ECF Nos. 10, 21, or
45 that would terminate a claim and that depends on the identity of the operative pleading;

(d) directing that the discovery objections presented here be determined before, or
expressly within, any adjudication that relies on the factual premises the interrogatories in ECF
Nos. 15-1 and 54-1 address;

(e) preserving the fifth objection and the concurrent targeted-vacatur application for
coordinated determination, without treating ownership of the reported interest or disqualification
as established; and

(f) expedited consideration of this request.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 89 Filed 10/13/26 Page 7 of 12 PagelD# 876

VI. RELIEF ON THE OBJECTIONS

16. Plaintiff requests an order, in the form of the accompanying Proposed Order:

(a) sustaining these objections and setting aside the rulings in ECF No. 84 denying ECF
Nos. 59, 15, and 54;

(b) granting ECF No. 76 and deeming the Notice at ECF No. 76-1 filed and considered;
determining the comparison-related objections in ECF Nos. 66 and 67 and the supporting issues in
ECF No. 68; and expressly reserving every other issue presented in ECF Nos. 66, 67, and 68 that
the order does not decide;

(c) removing the comparison condition in ECF No. 64 as a prerequisite to consideration of
ECF No. 59, and vacating the September 11, 2026 deadline;

(d) granting ECF No. 59 under Rules 15(a)(2) and 15(d); deeming ECF No. 59-1 filed as the
Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint and the operative pleading; directing separate
docketing; setting the time for responses; and directing how ECF Nos. 10, 21, and 45 will be
handled in light of the operative pleading;

(e) alternatively to (d), restoring ECF No. 59 to pending status for determination under
Rules 15(a)(2) and 15(d) on its existing authorized submissions, including ECF Nos. 59, 59-1, 59-
2, 60, 74, 78, 78-1, 83, and, if leave is granted, 76 and 76-1, without an additional comparison;

(f) granting ECF Nos. 15 and 54 and authorizing service of the interrogatories at ECF Nos.
15-1 and 54-1 on the terms stated in those motions, with answers due seven calendar days after
service or within another period the Court directs;

(g) alternatively to (f), restoring ECF Nos. 15 and 54 to pending status for determination
under Rule 26(d)(1), with their authorized briefing preserved and their grounds based on the First

Amended Complaint intact independently of the disposition of ECF No. 59, including ECF Nos.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 89 Filed 10/13/26 Page 8 of 12 PagelD# 877

15, 15-1, 16, 31, 33, 36, 46, 52, 78, and 78-1 as to ECF No. 15, and ECF Nos. 54, 54-1, 55, 73, and
81 as to ECF No. 54; and

(h) determining the fifth objection in coordination with the concurrent Plaintiff’s Motion
for Targeted Vacatur of ECF Nos. 64 and 84, Withdrawal or Modification of the Magistrate-Judge
Referral, and Related Interim Relief, and identifying in the order which issues are decided, which
are reserved, and which are moot because complete relief has been granted on the preceding
objections. The pendency of the financial-conflict applications does not prevent the District Judge
from granting independently warranted relief on the preceding objections, and Plaintiff requests
that relief under paragraphs (a) through (g) without awaiting resolution of the financial-conflict
applications.

VII. POSITIONS PRESERVED
17. Plaintiff maintains that the First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5) independently states

each of its six claims and survives ECF Nos. 10, 21, and 45. Plaintiff maintains his entitlement to
amend and to supplement through ECF No. 59. Plaintiff maintains that ECF Nos. 15 and 54 are
supported on the First Amended Complaint and the existing record, whether or not leave to amend
is granted.

18. Nothing in this Motion revives ECF No. 26, which remains withdrawn (ECF No. 62), or
affects ECF Nos. 43, 70, and 71. Nothing in this Motion withdraws the objections in ECF Nos. 66
and 67 concerning the generative-artificial-intelligence provisions, the termination of oral
argument, or the remote-appearance motion (ECF No. 41), or resolves them by implication. The
hearings previously set on ECF Nos. 15 and 54 were terminated (ECF Nos. 63, 65); Plaintiff’s
request to restore argument on those motions (ECF No. 67 § 6(d)) remains pending.

VII. SUPPORTING RECORD

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 89 _ Filed 10/13/26 Page 9 of 12 PagelD# 878

19. Plaintiff submits with this Motion: the Memorandum in Support; a Proposed Interim
Order; a Proposed Order; an Alternative Proposed Order; and a Notice of Waiver of Oral
Argument. The first four objections rely on the existing record, including ECF Nos. 68-1, 59-2, and
31 and the docket. The fifth objection additionally relies on the Declaration of Marvelle J.
Ballentine in Support of Plaintiff’s Motion to Disqualify Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis and its
Exhibit A (Financial Disclosure Report, Calendar Year 2025) and Exhibit B (Financial Disclosure
Report, Calendar Year 2024), submitted with the concurrent disqualification motion and not yet
assigned docket numbers.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter the Proposed Interim
Order and, upon determination of these objections, the Proposed Order or, in the alternative, the

Alternative Proposed Order, granting the relief stated in paragraphs 15 through 16.
